classification.difficultyReason: Requires comparing parameter-dependent distance equation solution sets and distinguishing discrete solutions from intervals; the catalogue has no exact equation-set comparison skill.

content.prompt: What is the condition on $r$, in terms of $a$, if the solutions of $|x-a|=r$ are disjoint (share no common values) from the solutions of $|x+a|=r$?

answer.short:
For $r\ge0$, the sets are disjoint exactly when $a\ne0$ and $r\ne|a|$.

Compare the points $a\pm r$ and $-a\pm r$. If $r<0$, both sets are empty and hence disjoint.
answer.worked:
If $r<0$, neither equation has a solution, so the sets are disjoint.

For $r\ge0$, the distance definition gives the solution sets $\{a-r,a+r\}$ and $\{-a-r,-a+r\}$. A common value must satisfy one of
$$\begin{align*}a-r&=-a-r\quad\text{or}\quad a+r=-a+r\\a-r&=-a+r\quad\text{or}\quad a+r=-a-r.\end{align*}$$
The first row requires $a=0$. The second row requires $r=a$ or $r=-a$. Thus, for $r\ge0$, the sets are disjoint exactly when $a\ne0$ and $r\ne|a|$. In particular, $r>|a|$ still gives disjoint sets of points.
